paragraphs: Here is the big idea, baker. God finishes what He starts, and the whole sky knows it. The great multitude cries, "Hallelujah! For the Lord our God the Almighty reigns." (Revelation 19:6) Babylon looked huge and loud and unbeatable, and God still had the last word, and heaven shouted its thanks that His judgments are "true and just." (Revelation 19:2)

And look at what the shouting is aimed at. It's a wedding. "The marriage of the Lamb has come, and His bride has made herself ready." (Revelation 19:7) The fine linen she wears is "the righteous acts of the saints," (Revelation 19:8) so getting ready is real, daily work, and that's why my ovens stay warm. Now hear me, friend: "Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb." (Revelation 19:9) It's an invitation, and I know what it feels like to be invited when you figured nobody remembered you.

Then John falls at the angel's feet, and the angel says, "Do not do that!" (Revelation 19:10) He's a fellow servant, and the call is, "Worship God!" (Revelation 19:10) So here's what I'm taking with me, baker. Every bit of this points to Jesus, "the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy," (Revelation 19:10) so keep your eyes on Him, keep your apron ready, and let the praise go where it belongs. The story of Babylon ends here, but the Supper is still coming, and I will NOT be the one who gets the credit.
